UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday that the rapid expansion of artificial‑intelligence systems must be met with stronger regulatory safeguards, joining a wave of international voices urging tighter oversight. In a statement delivered to the UN Human Rights Council, Türk warned that unchecked AI development could evolve into an “existential risk to humanity,” echoing concerns raised by governments, industry groups and civil‑society organizations over the technology’s potential to amplify discrimination, undermine privacy and destabilise global security.

Türk’s remarks come as the United Nations prepares to convene a high‑level forum on digital governance later this year, where member states are expected to discuss a coordinated framework for AI accountability and transparency. The chief highlighted the need for binding standards that address both the ethical use of AI and the protection of fundamental rights, urging policymakers to act before the technology’s capabilities outpace existing legal safeguards. The call for coordinated action reflects a broader consensus that proactive, multilateral regulation is essential to mitigate the long‑term risks posed by advanced AI systems.
author: UN News

title: Three men on trial for killing Australian surfers and American in Baja California
content:
Three men have begun a criminal trial in the resort town of La Paz, Baja California, for the 2024 murders of Australian brothers Jake (30) and Callum Robinson (33) and their American companion Jack Carter Rhoad (30). The trio was shot dead after an alleged robbery while surfing at a popular beach in the Mexican state, an incident that drew international attention and highlighted the region’s rising crime rates. Prosecutors allege that the defendants, all Mexican nationals, opened fire on the victims as they disembarked from their surfboards, subsequently stealing personal belongings and fleeing the scene.

The trial, held in a court that serves both local residents and the influx of tourists drawn to the area’s surf culture, will consider forensic evidence, eyewitness testimony and video footage captured by nearby beachgoers. Authorities have emphasized that the proceedings aim to deliver justice and deter future violent crimes targeting foreign visitors. The defendants remain in custody pending a verdict, which is expected later this year.
author: Guardian World

title: Israel says it captured ridge in Lebanon, affecting peace talks
content:
Israel’s ongoing air and artillery strikes along the Israel‑Lebanon border have intensified pressure on Beirut’s efforts to secure a long‑sought peace agreement and maintain domestic stability. The attacks, which have targeted positions linked to Hezbollah and other militant groups, come amid stalled negotiations between Lebanese political factions and international mediators who have been trying to formalize a cease‑fire framework that would end years of intermittent conflict.

The renewed hostilities have disrupted diplomatic talks that were scheduled for the coming weeks, prompting the Lebanese government to call for an emergency session of its cabinet and to appeal to the United Nations for a renewed monitoring mission. Analysts note that the escalation threatens to undermine fragile economic reforms and could exacerbate sectarian tensions within Lebanon, complicating the country’s path toward a sustainable political settlement. International observers stress that de‑escalation is essential for both nations to resume dialogue and achieve a durable peace.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kosovo joins US‑led Gaza stabilisation force
content:
A Balkan state has announced its intention to join a small group of nations that have pledged to contribute peacekeeping personnel to the Palestinian enclave of Gaza. The foreign ministry of Serbia confirmed that it will provide a contingent of troops to a United Nations‑mandated mission aimed at stabilising the territory in the aftermath of the recent armed conflict, marking the country's first commitment of this kind to the region.

Serbia’s decision follows similar pledges from Norway, Ireland, Spain, Sweden and Finland, all of which have expressed willingness to deploy forces under a UN framework that seeks to protect civilians, facilitate humanitarian aid and monitor cease‑fire arrangements. The Serbian delegation indicated that the size and composition of its contribution will be coordinated with the UN Department of Peace Operations and will be contingent on the establishment of a clear mandate and security conditions on the ground. By joining the short list of contributing countries, Serbia aims to support international efforts to restore order and assist in the reconstruction of Gaza, while reinforcing its broader diplomatic engagement with multilateral peace initiatives.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rising soup costs double in Nigeria, making family meals less affordable
content:
Lagos, Nigeria — A recent comment from a local market vendor highlighted the steep rise in food costs, noting that “5,000 naira used to make a pot of soup, now 10,000 naira isn’t enough.” The observation reflects broader price pressures across the country, where the Consumer Price Index has climbed by more than 30 % over the past year, driven largely by higher prices for staples such as rice, beans and cooking oil. Traders in major urban centers report that the cost of basic ingredients has doubled, forcing many households to cut portions or switch to cheaper, lower‑quality alternatives.

Economists attribute the surge to a combination of factors, including weakened naira exchange rates, increased import tariffs on essential commodities, and disruptions in regional supply chains caused by climatic events. The federal government has announced a series of measures aimed at stabilising prices, such as subsidies for fertilizer, accelerated agricultural investment, and temporary price caps on selected food items. Analysts caution that while these steps may provide short‑term relief, sustained affordability will depend on longer‑term reforms in production, distribution and monetary policy.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Serbian government announces snap election and dissolution of parliament
content:
Belgrade is preparing for a national election that many analysts describe as a strategic effort by President Aleksandar Vučić to consolidate his authority after a prolonged wave of street demonstrations. The vote, scheduled for early 2024, follows months of large‑scale protests sparked by accusations of media suppression, alleged electoral irregularities and growing concerns over the government’s commitment to democratic norms. Opposition parties, which have struggled to unite behind a single candidate, have called for international monitoring and urged voters to reject the ruling Serbian Progressive Party’s (SNS) bid for a third consecutive term.

International observers note that the election will test Serbia’s relationship with the European Union, which has repeatedly urged the government to guarantee a level playing field and protect civil liberties. While the SNS remains dominant in parliament and controls key state institutions, the recent unrest has pressured Vučić to present a more open electoral process, including promises of greater transparency and limited media access for rivals. The outcome will determine whether the current administration can further tighten its grip on power or face renewed demands for reform from a populace still mobilized by the recent protests.
author: Al Jazeera

title: B’Tselem executive director labels Gaza conflict genocide
content:
Jerusalem – B’Tselem, the Israeli nonprofit that monitors human‑rights conditions in the occupied Palestinian territories, announced today the appointment of Dr. Hadas Ziv as its new executive director, succeeding longtime chief Yossi Amrani. Ziv, a former senior analyst at the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs and author of several reports on civilian protection, will assume the post on 1 October, overseeing the organization’s research, advocacy, and outreach programs.

The leadership change comes as B’Tselem prepares to release its annual report on civilian casualties and settlement expansion, topics that have drawn heightened international scrutiny. In a statement, the board highlighted Ziv’s extensive experience in international law and her commitment to the organization’s mission of documenting violations and promoting accountability. Ziv’s appointment is expected to maintain B’Tselem’s operational continuity while potentially broadening its engagement with diplomatic and legal forums.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bolivia military base blasts kill seven, rescue search continues
content:
President Rodrigo Paz announced a period of national mourning on Thursday after a series of explosions ripped through a military installation on the outskirts of La Paz, killing at least 27 soldiers and wounding dozens more. The blasts, which officials say were caused by an accidental detonation of stored munitions, struck the 5th Infantry Brigade’s ammunition depot during routine maintenance, prompting an immediate emergency response that included fire crews, medical teams and security forces to secure the site and prevent further casualties.

In a televised address, President Paz urged citizens to remain calm and united, emphasizing that the tragedy underscores the need for stricter safety protocols within the armed forces and for continued support of the families affected. He ordered flags to be flown at half‑mast nationwide and directed the Ministry of Defense to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident’s causes, while pledging that the government will allocate additional resources for medical care and compensation for the victims. The president’s call for solidarity aims to reinforce national cohesion as the country mourns the loss and works toward preventing similar accidents in the future.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nauru opens embassy in Jerusalem
content:
Pacific island nation Nauru announced on Monday that it has opened an embassy in Jerusalem, making it the ninth country to establish a diplomatic mission in the Israeli capital. The move follows similar decisions by nations such as the United States, Guatemala, Honduras, Kosovo, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco and Paraguay, which have placed their embassies in Jerusalem in recent years. Nauru’s foreign ministry said the new embassy will strengthen bilateral ties, facilitate cooperation in areas including trade, tourism and technology, and reflect the island’s support for Israel’s claim to the city.

The establishment of the embassy comes amid ongoing international debate over the status of Jerusalem and its recognition as a capital. While many countries maintain embassies in Tel Aviv pending a negotiated settlement to the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict, Nauru’s decision aligns it with a growing group of states that have formally recognized Jerusalem as Israel’s capital. Officials from both governments indicated that the diplomatic upgrade is expected to deepen mutual engagement and further integrate Nauru into regional and global diplomatic networks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two Egyptian wrestlers flee abroad, face legal threats
content:
Two wrestlers have become the latest athletes to flee while abroad, prompting an outpouring of sympathy from international observers and sparking legal threats from officials in their home country. The pair left the nation where they were competing and sought refuge in a foreign jurisdiction, citing personal safety concerns and political pressures as primary motivations for their departure. Their sudden disappearance has been confirmed by local authorities, who have opened investigations into the circumstances surrounding the exit.

The incident adds to a growing pattern of sports figures seeking asylum or avoiding prosecution by leaving their native lands, a trend that has drawn criticism from governments that view such actions as betrayals. Legal representatives of the wrestlers’ home nation have warned of potential extradition requests and criminal charges, while human‑rights groups have called for protection of the athletes’ rights to freedom of movement and expression. The situation remains under close watch as diplomatic channels assess possible resolutions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Grindr agrees to pay £26 million to settle UK privacy lawsuit
content:
A long‑standing allegation contends that the dating app Grindr violated United Kingdom privacy legislation by disclosing users’ personal information to third‑party organisations without adequate legal basis. The claim, which has been referenced in multiple regulatory inquiries, asserts that Grindr’s data‑sharing practices breach the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK‑GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018, which require explicit user consent and transparent processing for any transfer of personal data.

Regulators, including the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), have examined the accusations, focusing on whether Grindr’s disclosures to advertisers, analytics providers and other partners were sufficiently justified under the law. Grindr has responded by stating that its data‑handling procedures comply with applicable privacy standards and that any sharing is performed in accordance with its privacy policy and user agreements. The ICO’s investigation remains ongoing, and the outcome will determine whether enforcement action or remedial measures are required to address the alleged infractions.
author: BBC World

title: Thousands attend funeral of convicted Bosnian war criminal Ratko Mladic in Serbia
content:
Former Bosnian Serb commander Radovan Mlađić, sentenced to life imprisonment for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the 1990s Bosnian conflict, remains a focal point of regional tension as the European Union cautioned Belgrade against any public glorification of the convicted war criminal. The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia found Mlađić responsible for the 1995 Srebrenica massacre and the siege of Sarajevo, and he has been incarcerated in a high‑security prison in The Hague since his 2017 conviction.

In a statement issued this week, the EU warned that attempts to honor Mlađić—through commemorative events, monuments or public rhetoric—would breach Serbia’s accession commitments and could impede its EU integration process. The warning follows recent reports of gatherings in Serbian towns that praised the former leader, prompting diplomatic concerns in Brussels. EU officials emphasized that respect for the rule of law and the rights of victims must guide Serbia’s domestic policies, underscoring that any deviation could result in further scrutiny of the country's reform agenda.
author: BBC World

title: NASA Astronauts on ISS Take Labor Day Off
content:
NASA’s three astronauts aboard the International Space Station will take a scheduled break on Labor Day, mirroring the rest that Earth‑bound workers enjoy on the holiday. The crew, which includes NASA’s mission specialists and flight engineers, has been conducting routine maintenance, scientific experiments, and health monitoring since their arrival in late 2023.

The pause comes as part of the station’s standard operational cycle, allowing crew members to recharge after weeks of continuous activity. While the astronauts remain in orbit, the International Space Station will continue to support ongoing research and international collaboration, with ground teams coordinating the transition back to full operational status after the holiday break.
author: Space.com

title: Celestron FirstScope: 20% Off Beginner Telescope on Amazon
content:
Amazon is currently offering a 20 % discount on the Celestron FirstScope, a compact telescope designed for quick stargazing sessions. The FirstScope is marketed as an entry‑level instrument that delivers clear views of the moon, planets, and bright deep‑sky objects, making it a popular choice for both first‑time users and casual observers.

The telescope’s lightweight, portable design and straightforward setup appeal to beginners and families with children. Its 2‑inch aperture and built‑in eyepiece provide a simple, low‑maintenance experience, while the included tripod and star chart help users locate celestial targets with ease. Celestron’s reputation for reliable optics and durable construction adds confidence for those new to astronomy.

With the discount in place, the FirstScope becomes an accessible entry point for amateur stargazers. The reduced price, combined with its user‑friendly features, positions the telescope as an attractive option for anyone looking to explore the night sky without a steep learning curve.
author: Space.com
